account:
Today I kept morning office hours and went to the mill for the ten o'clock grain inspection. I have now reached home for lunch, at 12:24; council letters at the office are next at 13:00. The inspection was inconclusive: no one showed me grain stocks, the appointment names no host, and neither the secretary nor builder could identify the mill operator. I asked the secretary to record it as incomplete and arrange a follow-up with the operator, not to treat it as a satisfactory inspection.

The unusual feature is how many townsfolk repeat almost the same vague report of a 'bridge or port change at the bakery.' One nearby townsman associated the report with the baker and neighbour being there. No one has explained an actual change, named its organizer, or produced evidence of damage. The builder says he is checking rumours, not reporting confirmed damage. Yesterday he likewise reported no confirmed defects at the bridge, landing, or warehouse approach. I have authorized neither works nor expenditure.

The baker offered bread for meetings this morning, but I placed no order. He said he knew of no gatherings and reported that the innkeeper had no guests or bread orders. Townspeople have seen him carrying a sack of bread at the bakery and on the west side of the square. That could be ordinary trade; it is not evidence of a secret gathering. Still, the repetition of an unexplained report involving transport and the bakery deserves a direct conversation with the baker and neighbour. It may concern a proposed change to crossings or deliveries, or simply be circulating gossip. I do not yet know its purpose or whether anything organized is happening without me. The secretary is helping with appointments and inquiries, but has no verified explanation either.
